highlights: Delivery momentum was strong: 2 of 3 MVP tasks were completed, including chief routing stabilization and the inbox acknowledgement patch.
You completed 4 of 5 logged sessions, and the interrupted prompt-review block was later recovered with a successful refinement session.
Recovery signals improved by the end of the period: sleep increased from 330 to 405 minutes, stress shifted from tense to neutral, and video fatigue eased.
blockers: Recovery work lagged behind delivery: the recovery goal is still at 0 of 2 completed tasks.
Meeting-heavy windows increased tension and caused at least one interrupted focus block, which lined up with lower focus and mood.
The missed-call review remains blocked, and the sleep trend check received effort but still lacks a clear closeout.
trends: Focus started high, dropped when interruptions rose, and then partially recovered when work was reduced to smaller blocks.
Energy stayed fragile through the week; short sleep and late-sprint fatigue repeatedly pulled attention and mood down.
End-of-week signals were modestly better than midweek, with higher sleep, lower audio stress, and better video-based focus than the prior day.
nextSuggestions: Finish the in-progress prompt review early next week, before new work is added to the delivery track.
Give the recovery goal one clear win next week by turning the sleep trend check into a small written output and scheduling a 15-minute slot to unblock the missed-call review.
Protect one low-interruption block before meetings, keep work in shorter restart-friendly chunks, and add a brief walk or screen break when fatigue spikes.
